name: PESTLE Analysis
problem: Provides a framework for investigating and analyzing external macro-environmental influences operating outside an organization's control, reducing uncertainty regarding future environmental threats and opportunities.
when_not: When analysing short-term operational tweaks without external market or environmental dependency, or when immediate low-risk hypotheses need rapid execution.
outputs: Categorized list of key external influences, SWOT opportunities and threats.
decisions: Strategic direction, market positioning, compliance strategies, product strategy.

name: Porter's Five Forces
problem: Determines the competitive intensity and profitability of an industry or market domain, reducing strategic blind spots regarding industry competitive pressures.
when_not: In non-competitive internal process optimization or when analyzing internal team dynamics/operations.
outputs: Industry pressure assessment, competitive position summary, SWOT opportunities and threats.
decisions: Market entry/exit, competitive strategy, pricing strategy, business model selection.

name: Benchmarking and Market Analysis
problem: Reduces uncertainty about competitive standing, market trends, and organizational efficiency gaps by comparing internal performance against external baselines or market demands.
when_not: When seeking novel, ground-breaking innovations (benchmarking only reproduces existing practices), or when fast action is required on immediate hypotheses without market research budget.
outputs: Gap analysis report, market research summary, best practice recommendations, RFI evaluation.
decisions: Market entry/exit decisions, capability investment priorities, solution selection, change strategy definition.

name: SWOT Analysis
problem: Consolidates and synthesizes internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats, reducing unstructured, subjective strategy formulation. Reduces strategic blind spots by evaluating an organization's internal Strengths and Weaknesses alongside external Opportunities and Threats. No holistic view of the organisation's position
uncertainty: Not understanding external threats and internal weaknesses
when_not: As a standalone technique without prior formal environmental and internal capability analysis. For micro-level software component specification where enterprise strategy and environment are irrelevant. Local technical tasks within an existing product
outputs: SWOT Matrix, strategic options for development and evaluation. SWOT Matrix (2x2 grid: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats), strategic action strategies (SO, ST, WO, WT strategies). Result: SWOT matrix (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats). Artifacts: SWOT matrix, strategic initiatives
decisions: Strategic options identification, change initiative initiation, business case development. Strategic direction selection, change strategy formulation, business case justification. Scope, priority, business case

name: Boston Box
problem: Evaluates product and service portfolios based on market share and market growth, reducing bad investment decisions in non-performing assets.
when_not: For single-product startups or non-commercial internal IT systems without market competition.
outputs: 2x2 Matrix mapping products into Star, Cash Cow, Wild Cat/Problem Child, and Dog quadrants.
decisions: Product portfolio investment, divestment, resource allocation, release priorities.

name: Ansoff's Matrix
problem: Structures product and market growth strategies, reducing uncertainty when identifying alternatives for strategic expansion.
when_not: When analyzing purely internal process optimizations or non-growth compliance projects.
outputs: 2x2 Growth Strategy Matrix (Market Penetration, Market Development, Product Development, Diversification).
decisions: Scope definition, product roadmap decisions, market expansion strategy.

name: MOST Analysis
problem: Examines strategic direction alignment, ensuring tactics and operational efforts directly support higher-level mission and objectives, reducing strategic misalignment and conflicting priorities.
when_not: When performing pure low-level technical bug fixing or minor isolated operational changes with no strategic impact.
outputs: MOST Matrix/Statement (Mission, Objectives, Strategy, Tactics), identified organizational strengths and weaknesses.
decisions: Scope definition, strategy validation, change prioritization, project initiation.

name: Business Objectives, Vision and Scope
aliases: Defining Business Objectives (Vision and Scope / Business Objectives Model)
problem: Eliminates lack of alignment among stakeholders, prevents scope creep, and avoids building extraneous features that do not contribute to organizational value.
when_not: When working on minor maintenance tasks, localized bug fixes, or minor refactoring where organizational strategy is unaffected.
outputs: Vision and Scope Document (or Project Charter), Business Objectives Model (RML diagram), Objective Chain, Vision Statement, Success Metrics list.
decisions: Project chartering, funding/investment decisions, high-level scope inclusion/exclusion, feature prioritization alignment.

name: Critical Success Factors and KPIs
aliases: Critical success factors and key performance indicators
problem: Defines vital areas of performance and specific quantitative metrics to monitor progress toward organizational objectives, reducing ambiguity in performance evaluation. Reduces performance evaluation subjectivity by defining quantifiable indicators to track solution performance and strategic progress over time.
when_not: When managing ad-hoc, exploratory research projects where quantifiable outcomes cannot be pre-defined. When data collection costs vastly outweigh the value of monitoring, or when measuring purely ad-hoc creative activities.
outputs: CSF list (Industry-wide and Organization-specific), KPI targets with defined timeframes. KPI framework, target metrics, monitoring & evaluation plan, performance dashboards/reports.
decisions: Performance management, business case evaluation, project success verification. Solution performance evaluation, strategy adjustment, process optimization investments.

name: Balanced Scorecard
problem: Balances financial metrics with non-financial drivers of future success, reducing short-sighted over-reliance on past financial performance. Mitigates narrow financial focus by balancing performance evaluation across four perspective dimensions: Financial, Customer, Business Process, and Learning & Growth.
when_not: For single minor feature enhancement projects without broad organizational reach. For small, isolated tactical projects where organizational strategic alignment is not relevant or where no overarching business strategy exists.
outputs: Balanced Business Scorecard (BBS) covering Financial, Customer, Internal Business Process, and Learning & Growth perspectives. Balanced Scorecard matrix/dashboard, strategy map, target KPIs, performance reports.
decisions: Strategic performance monitoring, project portfolio selection, business model evaluation. Strategic investment decisions, project portfolio prioritization, organizational alignment, operational change strategy.

name: KPI Modelling (KPIM)
problem: Reduces misalignment and wrong prioritization by directly quantifying process efficiency gains and linking requirements to measurable business metrics.
when_not: When metrics data cannot be measured, or when process automation scope is trivial and metrics-driven trade-offs are unnecessary.
outputs: KPIM diagrams (process models with KPI annotations overlaid on specific steps), prioritized requirement lists.
decisions: Requirement prioritization decisions, release scope decisions, trade-off decisions between competing performance attributes.

name: Business Model Canvas
problem: Reduces strategic misalignment by mapping on a single page how an enterprise creates, delivers, and captures value across operational, financial, and customer dimensions. No holistic understanding of how the business creates value
uncertainty: Fragmented elements of a new product's business logic
when_not: For micro-level technical tasks or isolated software feature specs with no impact on the overall business model. Internal technical refactoring of systems
outputs: Business Model Canvas (9 building blocks), diagnostic assessment, target business model blueprint. Result: completed canvas of the 9 business model blocks. Artifacts: Business Model Canvas diagram
decisions: Strategic pivot decisions, target operating model selection, product-market fit evaluation. Scope, business case, architecture

name: Value Proposition Analysis
problem: Analyzes customer perspectives on value across Timing, Financial, and Quality categories for Owners, Partners, and End Customers, reducing misalignment between business processes and customer expectations.
when_not: For purely technical internal infrastructure maintenance projects with no customer-facing or commercial dimensions.
outputs: Value Proposition Matrix mapping customer types against value categories.
decisions: Business process redesign priorities, service level target setting, product positioning.

name: Opportunity Canvas
problem: Reduces strategic uncertainty and risk of building features that fail to achieve business impact or solve real user problems; prevents accepting low-value ideas into product development.
when_not: Small bug fixes, clear maintenance tasks, well-understood minor refinements with minimal cost and risk.
outputs: Opportunity Canvas (9-box structure summarizing problems, users, solutions, user value, metrics, adoption, business metrics, and budget), Go/No-Go decision.
decisions: Go/No-Go discovery initiation, budget allocation, target customer segment selection, metric alignment.

name: Impact Mapping
problem: Prevents building the wrong software, waste of time and money due to wrong assumptions, scope creep, over-engineered solutions, lack of alignment with business objectives, pet features, ad-hoc prioritisation, and poor communication between business stakeholders and technical delivery teams.
when_not: Not applicable to maintenance-mode projects without strategic goals, projects with no access to business decision-makers, or environments with rigid fixed-scope/fixed-cost contracts that forbid adaptive planning.
outputs: Impact Map (mind-map/diagram), metrics table, SMART goal definitions, milestone plans, and refined user stories.
decisions: Scope decisions, milestone roadmap decisions, feature prioritization, architecture/solution design trade-offs, release planning, and investment allocation (incremental funding).

name: Resource Audit
problem: Identifies internal resource capability, highlights core competencies, and uncovers weaknesses that could prevent or undermine business change.
when_not: In small-scale, rapid hypothesis testing where resource constraints are well understood or negligible.
outputs: Resource Audit profile categorized by Physical, Financial, Human, Reputation, and Know-how resources.
decisions: Feasibility decisions, build vs. buy, investment decisions, resource allocation.

name: McKinsey 7-S
problem: Ensures holistic organizational alignment across 7 core areas during business change, reducing implementation failures caused by misaligned soft/hard factors.
when_not: For isolated, localized software tweaks that have zero impact on staff, structure, or management culture.
outputs: 7-S Alignment Audit Report, impact analysis, change initiative recommendations.
decisions: Target Operating Model design, organizational restructuring, change management strategy.

name: Leavitt's Diamond
problem: Analyzes proposed organizational changes holistically across four interdependent components, preventing project failure caused by isolated technological or structural changes.
when_not: For minor bug fixes or minor localized routine maintenance tasks.
outputs: Impact analysis matrix across Task, Structure, People, and Technology.
decisions: Implementation planning, change impact scope, training and organizational restructuring plans.

name: Capability Modelling
problem: Models what an organization needs to do to deliver value, independent of how, who, or where it is executed, reducing duplication and stability issues in business transformation. Reduces organizational misalignment and duplication by defining what an enterprise can do independent of how it is executed or structured.
when_not: When analyzing short-term procedural task sequences or temporary project task steps. For micro-level bug fixes or minor tactical changes where enterprise-level alignment offers no value.
outputs: Hierarchical Business Capability Model (Strata, Foundation, Capability Groups, Business Capabilities taxonomy). Capability Map, performance gap assessment, risk model, product/release roadmap.
decisions: Target Operating Model design, enterprise architecture alignment, application portfolio rationalization, outsourcing decisions. Strategic investment allocation, IT portfolio prioritization, M&A integration scope, release planning.

name: Value Chain Analysis
problem: Groups organizational activities into Primary (Inbound logistics, Operations, Outbound logistics, Marketing/Sales, Service) and Support activities, reducing siloed operational thinking.
when_not: When analyzing micro-level algorithmic system code or localized single-task desk procedures.
outputs: Value Chain Diagram showing primary and support activity chains.
decisions: Process hierarchy structuring, process improvement prioritization, target operating model design.

name: Value Streams
problem: Models end-to-end sequential stages that deliver value to stakeholders, reducing siloed process optimization that fails to deliver end-to-end value.
when_not: For micro-level task step analysis or purely technical system integration mapping.
outputs: Value Stream Model depicting sequential value stages, trigger events, and enabling business capabilities.
decisions: Customer experience optimization, process re-engineering scope, capability investment prioritization.

name: POPIT Model
problem: Provides an holistic framework for identifying required business changes across four key dimensions, preventing single-dimensional (e.g. IT-only) project failure.
when_not: For trivial bug fixes or micro-level task edits that carry no broader organizational impact.
outputs: POPIT Change Assessment across Processes, Organization, People, and Information/Technology.
decisions: Business case option design, change impact scope, target operating model specification.

name: Organisation Modelling
problem: Integrates external environment factors (PESTLE, Competitors, Suppliers, Customers) with the internal Value Chain, providing complete organizational context for process improvement. Reduces structural misalignment and communication gaps by defining roles, responsibilities, reporting hierarchies, and formal/informal interaction networks.
when_not: When analyzing a minor, isolated internal software utility with no external environmental dependencies. On small, single-team software bug fixes where organizational structures have zero impact.
outputs: Completed Organisation Diagram showing external forces surrounding the internal Value Chain. Organizational Charts (Org Charts), Matrix Models, role descriptions, interface definitions, influencer network map.
decisions: Process improvement context setting, organizational alignment, project scope boundary setting. Organizational redesign, change management planning, governance escalation paths, role authority allocation.

name: Gap Analysis
aliases: Gap Analysis for Replacement & Enhancement Systems
problem: Compares the current 'as is' business situation with the conceptual 'to be' desired model to identify required change actions across Process, IT, People, and Organization. Prevents missing vital legacy functionality, carrying forward unnecessary 'junk' features, or creating operational disruptions when replacing or enhancing existing systems. Not understanding the difference between the current and the target state
when_not: When the project is a pure technical infrastructure replacement with zero change to business processes, human roles, or organization. For brand new 'green-field' projects with no existing legacy system baseline. Building a product from scratch (there is no current state)
outputs: Gap Analysis Report, categorized change actions list across POPIT (Process, IT, People, Organization). Gap Analysis Matrix / Feature Tree (categorized into: Requirements to Replicate, Requirements to Modify, Requirements to Add, Requirements to Drop) Result: list of gaps, plan for closing the gaps. Artifacts: gap matrix, list of transition requirements
decisions: Business case option formulation, change initiative scoping, target operating model design. Scope, release baseline, process change, architecture. Scope, architecture, release

name: Options Identification
problem: Generates a comprehensive longlist of potential business and technical solution options, preventing premature commitment to a single unexamined solution.
when_not: When the solution option is strictly dictated by mandatory statutory legal compliance with zero alternative choices.
outputs: Options Longlist covering business and technical possibilities (including 'Do Nothing').
decisions: Business case scope options, solution approach selection.

name: Feasibility Analysis
problem: Evaluates shortlisted options across Business, Technical, and Financial dimensions, reducing the risk of selecting unviable, unaffordable, or technically impossible options.
when_not: During initial creative brainstorming where feasibility filtering would stifle idea generation.
outputs: Feasibility Assessment Report evaluating shortlisted options against Business, Technical, and Financial criteria.
decisions: Option shortlisting, business case recommendation, risk identification.

name: Force-Field Analysis
problem: Identifies driving forces (+ positive) and restraining forces (- negative) acting upon a proposed change option, guiding strategies to strengthen drivers and reduce resistance.
when_not: When selecting purely technical algorithms where human/organizational forces are absent.
outputs: Force-Field Diagram mapping driving forces and restraining forces, with force-mitigation strategy.
decisions: Option selection, change management plan formulation, risk mitigation strategy.

name: Option Evaluation and Decision Analysis
aliases: Evaluating Alternative Options (Decision Making / NFR Framework)
Option Evaluation (Qualitative NFR & Quantitative Weighted Matrices)
problem: Reduces arbitrary or sub-optimal decision making when choosing among competing system proposals, goal refinements, responsibility assignments, or architecture styles. Reduces decision uncertainty when choosing among alternative goal refinements, architectural options, risk countermeasures, or responsibility assignments. Reduces decision bias and uncertainty when evaluating complex, high-risk alternatives with conflicting objectives and multi-criteria outcomes. Provides a quantitative, objective scoring framework to select the best solution alternative among competing options.
when_not: When there is only one feasible way to satisfy a requirement, or when options carry identical risk and quality profiles. When one option is strictly mandatory due to absolute legal, regulatory, or hard technical constraints. When decisions must be made instantaneously in emergencies, or when information is too scarce to establish meaningful criteria. When decision criteria cannot be quantified or when stakeholders agree informally without complex math.
outputs: NFR contribution graphs, qualitative satisficing labels (++, +, -, --, S, D, C, U), weighted decision matrices, selected 'best' option proposal. NFR contribution tables (+/++/-/-- labels), weighted decision matrices, selected 'best' system option. Simple/weighted decision matrices, decision trees, trade-off rankings, recommended action report. Completed decision matrix table with numerical scores and winning option
decisions: Architecture style selection, automation boundary decisions, goal refinement path selection. System boundary selection, architectural style choice, conflict resolution trade-offs. Vendor selection, design option selection, change strategy recommendations, risk treatment response. Architecture selection, feature baseline inclusion, vendor choice.

name: Plus-Minus-Interesting (PMI)
problem: Evaluates proposed solution alternatives objectively by categorizing positive, negative, and uncertain repercussions.
when_not: When quantitative decision criteria (e.g., monetary weights) are strictly required.
outputs: PMI table, categorized impact report
decisions: Alternative selection, conflict resolution.

name: Optioneering (Trade-Off Analysis)
problem: Selects the optimal system design architecture among competing alternatives that best satisfies conflicting stakeholder requirements within cost, risk, and technical limits.
when_not: When only one technical solution is feasible or pre-mandated by law/policy.
outputs: Trade-off evaluation matrix, QOC diagrams, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) biplots, output-prioritized product specification, baseline design selection rationale
decisions: System architecture selection, vendor selection, release scope baseline, output priority assignment.

name: Ready-Made / COTS Solution Selection
problem: Prevents organizations from buying ready-made software that fails to fit their business processes, or incurring unexpected, massive customization costs. Prevents acquiring expensive packaged software that fails to meet business needs, exhibits data model disconnects, or requires excessive custom extension.
when_not: Building 100% custom, highly proprietary core IP algorithms with zero commercial software equivalents. When custom software development is already mandated or when purchasing minor, low-cost utility tools.
outputs: Request for Proposal (RFP) / Request for Information (RFI), Vendor Evaluation Matrix/Scoring Sheet, Fit-Gap Analysis, Purpose-Based Alignment Quadrant. Weighted COTS Evaluation Matrix (rows = weighted requirements, columns = candidate COTS packages, cells = scores/match comments)
decisions: Software procurement, Build vs Buy vs Borrow decisions, vendor selection, customization budget approval. Procurement/Buy vs. Build, vendor selection, architecture, scope.

name: Vendor Assessment
problem: Reduces third-party procurement risk by formally evaluating vendor stability, capability, licensing models, and compliance before committing to a commercial solution.
when_not: When building an in-house custom solution with no third-party software, hardware, or consulting vendor involvement.
outputs: Vendor assessment report, vendor scorecard, licensing/pricing model comparison, risk evaluation.
decisions: Vendor selection, commercial software procurement, outsourcing contracts, SLA approval.

name: Feasibility Assessment and Business Case Development
problem: Reduces financial, technical, and business uncertainty before committing resources to a change initiative.
when_not: When changes are minor, low-risk, or strictly mandated by legal/compliance requirements with no alternative implementation routes.
outputs: Business Case, Feasibility Report, CARDI/RAID log, Investment Appraisal (NPV, IRR, Payback), Benefits Plan.
decisions: Scope, financial commitment, project go/no-go, option selection.

name: Business Case
problem: Reduces financial and strategic uncertainty by providing a formal justification for investing resources in a proposed solution compared to alternative options or doing nothing. Assembles all analytical findings, option evaluations, cost-benefit models, and impact/risk assessments into a structured, convincing written business report for executive decision-makers. Reduces financial uncertainty, politically motivated project selection, and unclear business value/feasibility. No justification of whether an investment is worthwhile
uncertainty: Uncertainty about payback and financial value
when_not: For small, mandatory low-cost changes (e.g., urgent regulatory patch) where the cost of writing the business case exceeds the change cost. When presenting micro-level operational tweaks where a simple verbal briefing or email request is sufficient. Small-scale, low-risk, internal ad-hoc bug fixes or minor enhancements with guaranteed zero financial exposure. Mandatory regulatory (compliance) requirements where there is no choice
outputs: Business Case document/presentation (containing need assessment, desired outcomes, alternative analysis, and recommended solution). Written Business Case Report (Introduction, Management Summary, Background, Options, Benefits & Costs, Investment Appraisal, Impacts, Risks, Recommendations, Appendices). Vision Document, Business Case (cash flow analysis, ROI). Result: business case document with ROI, NPV and payback period. Artifacts: business case document, financial model
decisions: Project funding/approval, solution alternative selection, go/no-go change strategy decisions. Project authorization, capital expenditure approval, strategic option selection. Scope, project approval (go/no-go), release budget, priority. Scope, priority, release, business case

name: Business Case Presentation
problem: Delivers a short, sharp, persuasive executive briefing to decision-makers, summarizing the business case recommendations and securing approval.
when_not: When decision-makers require only a formal written report submission without a live meeting.
outputs: Slide Deck / Executive Presentation, approved business case decision.
decisions: Project authorization, budget sign-off, option selection.

name: 4As Communication Model
problem: Provides a 4-part planning structure (Aim, Audience, Arrangement, Appearance) for developing effective presentations and business documents.
when_not: For casual, informal 1-on-1 chats where formal communication planning is unnecessary.
outputs: Structured Presentation Plan / Document Layout (Aim, Audience analysis, Arrangement outline, Appearance specifications).
decisions: Presentation structure approval, document format design, communication strategy execution.

name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
problem: Identifies, quantifies, and contrasts the expected costs and benefits of a proposed solution option across Tangible/Intangible and Immediate/Longer-term categories. Evaluates project financial viability and compares hard monetary returns against soft quality factors to justify IT investments.
when_not: When evaluating mandatory regulatory options where execution is legally compulsory regardless of cost-benefit ratios. Mandatory legal/regulatory compliance projects where the system must be built regardless of cost.
outputs: Cost-Benefit Statement categorized by Tangible Immediate/Longer-term Costs and Tangible/Intangible Immediate/Longer-term Benefits. Cost/Benefit Table (Hard Benefits, Hard Costs, Net Present Value, Payback Period, Soft Factors score).
decisions: Business case financial justification, project authorization, option comparison. Project charter approval, go/no-go investment decisions, vendor selection.

name: Investment Appraisal and Financial Analysis
problem: Evaluates project options using quantitative financial models (Payback/Breakeven, Discounted Cash Flow / Net Present Value, Internal Rate of Return), proving financial viability. Reduces financial investment risk by evaluating expected costs, total cost of ownership (TCO), and projected value realization of solution options.
when_not: For non-financial mandatory compliance projects where options are dictated by law regardless of financial return. For minor, non-monetary operational tweaks where financial calculation overhead outweighs the change scope.
outputs: Financial Investment Appraisal Report showing Payback period, Net Present Value (NPV), and/or Internal Rate of Return (IRR). Cost-Benefit Analysis, ROI, Present Value (PV), Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Payback Period.
decisions: Project authorization, capital allocation, option selection. Capital allocation, solution recommendation, project continuation/cancellation (stage-gate review).

name: Benefits Categorisation
problem: Classifies business benefits into four distinct categories (Financial, Quantifiable, Measurable, Observable), providing a nuanced framework beyond simple tangible/intangible labels.
when_not: When preparing a simple informal rough estimate with no formal benefits management framework.
outputs: Categorized Benefits List (Financial, Quantifiable, Measurable, Observable) with defined evaluation mechanisms.
decisions: Business case justification, benefits management plan design, post-project evaluation criteria definition.

name: Business Impact Analysis
problem: Identifies and presents non-cost organizational, cultural, and procedural impacts of a proposed change, ensuring decision-makers have a complete picture beyond financial numbers.
when_not: For minor isolated technical bug fixes with zero process or human footprint.
outputs: Impact Analysis Report detailing non-cost impacts (Org structure, Interdepartmental relations, Working practices, Management style, Recruitment, Promotion, Customer focus, Supplier relations).
decisions: Business case approval, target operating model design, change management intervention planning.

name: Risk Analysis and Management
problem: Systematically identifies, assesses (impact & probability), and formulates responses/owners for risks threatening a proposed project option, increasing business case credibility. Reduces the negative impact of internal and external uncertainties on project and solution value by identifying, analyzing, evaluating, and planning risk responses.
when_not: During initial unconstrained creative brainstorming sessions. Never omitted entirely, though low-impact micro-tasks require only brief informal risk consideration.
outputs: Risk Log / Risk Matrix detailing Risk description, Impact (Large/Moderate/Small), Probability (High/Medium/Low), Response (Avoidance, Mitigation, Transference, Acceptance), and Risk Owner. Risk Register (Risk event, probability, impact, overall level, response strategy, risk owner, residual risk).
decisions: Business case authorization, contingency budget allocation, risk response planning. Change strategy selection, contingency budget allocation, solution go/no-go decisions.

name: Project Blastoff
problem: Prevents projects from rushing into presumed solutions, starting on vague foundations, or solving the wrong business problem.
when_not: Trivial low-risk bug fixes, routine operational maintenance, or simple predefined feature tweaks with fully known domain constraints.
outputs: Goal Statement (Purpose-Advantage-Measurement), Work Context Diagram, Stakeholder Map/Matrix, Business Event List, Risk List, Business Case.
decisions: Scope boundary, project Go/No-Go, budget allocation, initial release priority, stakeholder involvement strategy.

name: Situation Investigation and Problem Analysis
problem: Uncovers underlying root causes rather than symptoms of business problems, clarifies ambiguous problem statements, and resolves conflicting stakeholder perspectives.
when_not: When the issue is purely technical with zero business impact, or the root cause is completely known and verified.
outputs: Problem statement, Rich picture, Mind map, Fishbone diagram, Context diagram, project scope/ToR.
decisions: Scope, project initiation, project rejection.

name: Understanding the Problem Before the Solution
aliases: Understanding the Problem Before Converging on a Solution (Root Cause Analysis / Problem Statement)
problem: Prevents teams from building features or products that go unused or fail because they solve the wrong problem, address only symptoms, or jump prematurely to a suboptimal solution.
when_not: When the problem domain and root causes are already fully understood, clear, and validated by data, or for trivial low-risk bug fixes.
outputs: Root Cause Analysis Diagram (Fishbone / Ishikawa Diagram), Problem Statement document/section.
decisions: Scope definition, solution selection (e.g., build vs. buy, interim vs. long-term fix), project go/no-go.

name: Context-Free Problem Definition Questions
problem: Reduces ambiguity, misunderstandings, and misdirections when identifying the real business problem rather than jumping prematurely to a technical or biased solution.
when_not: When the core problem and scope are already completely verified, baselined, and legally/operationally mandated with zero ambiguity.
outputs: Validated problem statement, problem context, list of affected stakeholders, initial business risks, and high-level vision.
decisions: Scope determination, business case approval, decision to initiate or cancel a project.

name: Problem Determination Game
problem: Resolves multi-stakeholder conflicts, reduces noisy symptom lists, eliminates out-of-scope/unowned requests, and isolates the single real business problem to solve.
when_not: When there is already a single, clear, uncontested, and fully validated problem statement established.
outputs: A single validated real problem statement, lists of out-of-scope issues, identified risks, and implied requirements.
decisions: Project initiation, problem prioritization, product scope definition, business case development.

name: Product Scope Formula
problem: Defines explicit boundaries between project and product, mitigating scope creep and establishing clear decision criteria for project approval.
when_not: In extremely minor operational defect fixes where scope boundaries are completely self-evident and localized.
outputs: Product Scope Statement / Charter Section detailing problem, vision, acceptance criteria, functional goals, justifications, and constraints.
decisions: Project charter approval, budget allocation, release planning, scope change control.

name: Scope Modelling
problem: Reduces scope creep and boundary ambiguity by explicitly defining what elements fall inside and outside the limits of a change, solution, or business need.
when_not: On open-ended exploratory research initiatives where rigid boundaries impede initial ideation.
outputs: Scope models (Context Diagrams, In-Scope/Out-of-Scope lists, Use Case Diagrams, Feature breakdowns, Venn diagrams).
decisions: Contractual obligations, project estimation boundaries, requirement inclusion/exclusion, release planning.

name: Cynefin
problem: Categorizes business situations into 4 contexts (Simple, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic) to guide the selection of appropriate leadership, analysis, and decision-making approaches.
when_not: When the project approach and domain complexity are already thoroughly understood and fixed.
outputs: Categorized Situational Context (Simple, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic, or Disorder) and selected analytical/development approach.
decisions: Project lifecycle selection (Agile vs Waterfall), leadership style selection, decision-making approach.

name: Root Cause Analysis
problem: Prevents superficial symptom-fixing by systematically identifying and evaluating the underlying fundamental origin of a problem. Treating symptoms instead of eliminating the true cause
uncertainty: Not understanding the underlying nature of the problem
when_not: For simple, known one-off glitches where root cause is self-evident without investigation. The problem is obvious and needs an immediate fix
outputs: Fishbone (Ishikawa) Diagrams, 5 Whys analysis trace, corrective action plan. Result: cause-and-effect diagram, root cause. Artifacts: Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram, cause tree
decisions: Corrective action plan selection, process redesign priorities, quality improvement investments. Scope, architecture, priority

name: Five Whys
problem: Distinguishes superficial symptoms from underlying root causes during business problem investigation.
when_not: When the respondent lacks direct operational knowledge of the broader process domain, or when the problem is purely technical/structural and requires automated diagnostic logging.
outputs: Root cause statement, refined problem domain description.
decisions: Root cause confirmation, scope boundary decisions, solution feature prioritization.

name: Fishbone Diagram
problem: Identifies and categorizes the root causes of a specific business problem or undesirable effect, reducing superficial problem solving that only targets symptoms.
when_not: When the problem is simple, single-factor, and obvious without requiring multi-category diagnostic analysis.
outputs: Fishbone (Cause-and-Effect) Diagram mapping root causes into major categories.
decisions: Process improvement priorities, problem resolution strategy, business case problem statement.

name: Context Diagram
aliases: Defining the Solution's Boundaries (Context Diagram & Ecosystem Map)
problem: Defines the high-level scope and boundary of an IT or business system and its external interfacing actors, reducing scope creep and missed system interfaces. Defines product boundaries (scope) and reduces misunderstandings regarding external systems and user group interfaces. Eliminates scope creep by defining strict hard-system boundaries, external interfaces, and incoming/outgoing events. Reduces uncertainty regarding system scope, unaligned stakeholder expectations, and undefined external system interfaces. Prevents scope ambiguity, unbudgeted integration effort, interface mismatches, and uncoordinated upstream/downstream system impact.
when_not: When detailed internal process workflow or internal algorithmic logic needs to be documented. When the project scope is entirely isolated and has zero external actors or systems. When organizational problem boundaries remain ill-defined, highly political, or fluid. When the system scope and boundaries are already fully known and agreed upon by all stakeholders. When the project is a standalone application with zero external user classes, zero hardware interfaces, and zero external software integrations.
outputs: Context Diagram showing central system box, surrounding external actors (user roles, other systems, time), and association lines. Black-box system context diagram with external entities and data/event flows. Context diagram, in/out scope list, incoming/outgoing event inventory, condition-action tables, 'when' requirements Context Diagram, system boundary definition section. Context Diagram, Ecosystem Map, Release Objectives Table / Scope Statement.
decisions: System scope approval, interface architecture definition, project boundary agreement. Project scope boundaries, external API integration requirements, vendor responsibility boundaries. System architecture boundaries, project cost/effort estimation, interface contract definitions. Scope determination, preliminary architecture boundary decisions. Scope boundaries, release planning/roadmapping, system responsibility allocation, vendor interface constraints.

name: Problem Frames and Scope Diagrams
aliases: Context Diagrams and Problem Diagrams (Problem Frames)
System Scope Diagrams (Context, Problem, and Frame Diagrams)
problem: Reduces uncertainty regarding system scope, software-environment boundaries, shared phenomena, and misaligned machine assumptions. Reduces boundary ambiguity by defining the problem world components, the machine solution, shared interface phenomena, and the domain properties/requirements constraining them.
when_not: When system boundaries and environmental interfaces are already rigidly fixed and fully specified. For internal software architectural design where problem-world domain components are irrelevant.
outputs: Context diagrams, problem diagrams, instantiated frame diagrams. Context diagrams, Problem diagrams, instantiated Frame diagrams.
